scope: Theorem 5.1 (Maximal reduction) of the manuscript “The Penrose inequality for maximal asymptotically hyperbolic initial data” (preprints/The-Penrose-inequality-for-maximal-asymptotically-hyperbolic-initial-data-October-5-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 260 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 641d4aa3892adbca), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 26. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let F : [0, ∞) → [0, ∞) be continuous and nondecreasing. Suppose that every smooth, complete, connected, orientable, one-ended asymptotically hyperbolic three-dimensional exterior with nonempty compact minimal boundary, scalar curvature at least −6, g − b ∈ C2,γ τ for some 0 < γ < 1 and 3/2 < τ < 3, the weighted scalar integrability of Section 1, and four finite mass fluxes satisfies p0 ≥ F(Amin). The exponent γ may depend on the comparison metric. This hypothesis is to hold in every designated asymptotic chart, without a causal-character assumption on the mass covector. Then every maximal initial-data exterior of Section 1 satisfies, in each designated chart, p0(g) ≥ F (︁ Amin(S; g) )︁ .
